To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
attention spreads to more peripheral locations and overall sensitivity increases as a function of saccade preparation delay when the saccade goal is an extinguished target.
attentional resources are mainly focused at the sccade target and its surround, and that they spread to the periphery as a function of target visibility and saccade preparation.
attentional resources are spread over the visual field without dilution when preparing a saccadic eye movement to a previously extinguished stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the spatio-temporally dynamics of visual attention in the context of saccadic eye movements and its relation to the underlying neurophysiology.
the spatio-temporally dynamic allocation of attention in preparation for a saccade.
the spatio-temporally dynamic nature of the spread of attentional resources in the visual system and its relation to the underlying neural processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the spatial extent of attentional resources depends on the nature of the visual input. When the visual input is a structured stimulus, the focus of attentional resources is at the stimulus location.

the spatial distribution of attention in the perisaccadic period depends on the spatio-temporally dynamic properties of the visual receptive fields and the spatio-temporo-spatial properties of the visual stimulus.

the spatial spread of attention is a function of the spatio–temporal dynamics of the visual receptive fields and the behavioral consequences of this spread are a function of the spatial spread of the receptive fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatio-temporally dynamic nature of visual receptive fields is reflected in attentional spreading and in the absence of a trade-off between spatial spread and sensitivity.
attentional resources are allocated at the immediate vicinity of a visual cue when preparing a saccadic eye movement, but that they spread to a larger spatial area when the cue is no longer present.
attention is focused at the sacciade target and its surround when preparing a saccadic eye movement.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the preparation of a saccade towards a recently extinguish target does not result in an attentional focus at the saccadic goal.
the preparation of a saccade towards an extinguished target is accompanied by the spreading of attentional resources over a larger area without any trade-off in sensitivity.
the spatial spread of attentional resources is modulated by the spatiotemporal properties of the visual input.
